{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Reuse the existing Spring Integration Kafka channel adapter infrastructure (KafkaMessageDrivenChannelAdapter / Outbound channel adapter) as the baseline for U2–U5 rather than building a new client wrapper.",
    "Use Spring Boot's @ConfigurationProperties for Kafka concurrency and compression so global defaults are defined once and can be overridden per deployment via application.yml/properties (as required by U2).",
    "Expose consumer-side ACK/NACK through the existing Acknowledgment callback (MANUAL or MANUAL_IMMEDIATE ack mode) so U3 maps onto framework primitives instead of inventing a new mechanism.",
    "Implement U4 (bindRequestor / bindReplier) as a new Spring Integration Messaging Gateway pair with async reply semantics, modeled on the existing gateway abstraction.",
    "Implement U5 batching on top of Kafka producer batch.size / linger.ms settings plus a new channel-side aggregator option so users can choose producer-side or framework-side batching.",
    "For U1, use Testcontainers (embedded Kafka) and existing Spring Integration test patterns to make the acceptance suite part of the regular CI build.",
    "For Sqoop features (U6–U8), wrap the Sqoop CLI invocation in a dedicated Spring Integration adapter, passing Sqoop arguments through a configuration metadata class; do not implement a native Sqoop protocol client.",
    "Implement U6 (stop job) by issuing `sqoop job --exec <job> --stop` (or the documented stop mechanism) from a @ServiceActivator / control-bus operation.",
    "Implement U7 (logs) by launching Sqoop with output redirected to a Pipe and consuming the stream in a dedicated TaskExecutor, forwarding lines to SLF4J / the application logging system.",
    "Implement U8 (incremental load) by exposing the standard Sqoop `--incremental <mode>` and `--check-column` / `--last-value` parameters through the adapter's configuration."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "A single experienced Spring Integration developer (familiar with both the Kafka module and Spring's gateway abstractions) performs all work; no onboarding or ramp-up time is included.",
    "The existing Spring Integration Kafka module is already in the codebase and serves as the integration point; no greenfield project setup is required.",
    "Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6.x are available, matching the Spring 6.0 baseline mentioned in the specification.",
    "Unit tests are written incrementally inside each implementation activity and are not a separate top-level WBS item; only the Kafka acceptance test framework (U1) is its own activity because the user story specifically calls it out.",
    "No new CI infrastructure is built; the acceptance test work assumes the project's existing Maven/Gradle build can pick up Testcontainers-based tests.",
    "Apache Sqoop is assumed to be installed and reachable on the target host for the Sqoop stories; installing/configuring Sqoop itself is out of scope.",
    "Documentation is limited to reference docs (XSD/Adoc updates + a short sample) — not a full user guide or marketing material.",
    "Effort is expressed in ideal developer workdays (8 hours), excluding meetings, code review turnaround time, and unrelated overhead."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Requirements analysis and overall design",
      "activity_description": "Review all 8 user stories, reconcile U2's 'global defaults + per-deployment overrides' with Spring's configuration model, decide on adapter vs. gateway split for Kafka and Sqoop, and produce a short design note that drives the implementation activities."
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Kafka concurrency and compression support (U2)",
      "activity_description": "Add @ConfigurationProperties-backed defaults for consumer concurrency (concurrency property already exists, needs proper defaults + override semantics) and producer/consumer compression.type; wire them into the existing channel adapters; add unit tests covering override paths."
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Kafka ACK message option (U3)",
      "activity_description": "Expose a configuration flag to control manual acknowledgment behavior, propagate the Acknowledgment into the message handler chain, document the success/failure semantics, and add unit tests for both ack and nack flows."
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Kafka bindRequestor / bindReplier gateways (U4)",
      "activity_description": "Implement two new Spring Integration gateways (requestor producing with expected async reply, replier consuming requests and asynchronously sending replies) on top of Kafka topics, including correlation-key handling, reply timeout, and unit tests for happy path, timeout, and error reply."
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Kafka batching support (U5)",
      "activity_description": "Add a batching mode to the outbound Kafka adapter that aggregates messages either via producer-side batching settings or via a CorrelatingMessageHandler/aggregator before sending, and add unit tests verifying batch boundaries and error propagation."
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Kafka acceptance test suite for CI (U1)",
      "activity_description": "Introduce Testcontainers-based embedded Kafka tests that exercise send/receive, concurrency, compression, ACK, requestor/replier, and batching scenarios; wire them into the Maven build so they run on every CI build; fix any environment-related flakiness."
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Sqoop job stop support (U6)",
      "activity_description": "Add a stop operation to the Sqoop adapter (exposed as a Spring Integration control-bus operation or @ServiceActivator) that terminates a running job and releases resources; includes unit tests against a mock Sqoop invocation."
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Sqoop log capture and streaming (U7)",
      "activity_description": "Capture Sqoop's stdout/stderr by running the CLI in a process with piped streams, forward each line to SLF4J at an appropriate level, and make the log destination configurable; add unit tests verifying lines reach the application logger and that stream lifecycle is cleaned up on completion."
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Sqoop incremental data load support (U8)",
      "activity_description": "Expose Sqoop's `--incremental`, `--check-column`, and `--last-value` parameters through the adapter's configuration metadata, persist/load the last-value state across runs, and add unit tests covering append and lastmodified modes."
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Reference documentation and samples",
      "activity_description": "Update XSD/adoc reference documentation for the new Kafka attributes and the Sqoop adapter operations; add one short sample for each new feature so users can copy-paste a working configuration."
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Code review, integration testing, and bug fixing",
      "activity_description": "End-to-end review of all branches, run the full unit + acceptance test suite, fix issues found by review or by integration runs, and prepare the change set for release."
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 42
  }
}

- U5: Batching support
